title: Kebab koobideh
subtitle: Persian minced meat skewers
excerpt: Spiced minced lamb and onion pressed onto flat metal skewers and grilled over charcoal or under a hot grill. The most iconic of Persian kebabs, eaten with saffron rice and grilled tomatoes.
sourceNotes: Koobideh is the most widely made Persian kebab, found throughout Iran and in Iranian restaurants worldwide. Cross-referenced with Najmieh Batmanglij, Food of Life (2011) for spice blend and technique.

recipe.freezeNotes: Shaped, uncooked kebabs freeze for up to 1 month on their skewers. Grill from frozen, adding a few extra minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales well for a party. Skewer and chill up to 4 hours ahead.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The mixture must rest in the fridge for at least 1 hour to firm up before skewering.

content.text: Koobideh succeeds or fails on the fat content of the meat and the thorough kneading of the mixture. You need lamb with at least 20% fat, an onion grated and squeezed until almost dry, and enough handling that the mixture becomes a smooth paste that adheres to a flat metal skewer without slipping. Grill at high heat, turning just twice.

attrs.title: Skewers
attrs.body: Koobideh needs flat metal skewers, 2 to 3 cm wide, not round ones. The flat blade anchors the meat. If you only have round skewers, form the mixture into small oval patties instead and grill them flat on a rack.

items.prepNote: at least 20% fat; ask your butcher for shoulder mince
large, grated and squeezed very dry in a cloth
dissolved in 1 tbsp hot water, for basting

content.text: Grate the onion on the coarse side of a box grater. Wrap in a clean cloth and squeeze out as much moisture as possible. The onion should be almost dry.

Combine the lamb, squeezed onion, turmeric, black pepper, salt, and baking powder in a large bowl. Knead with your hands for 5 full minutes until the mixture is smooth, slightly sticky, and holds its shape when pressed. It should feel almost like a paste.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight.

Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions. Wet your hands. Take a portion and press it firmly around a flat metal skewer, forming a cylinder about 15 cm long and 3 cm across. The meat must grip the skewer; press firmly at each end. Repeat with all portions.
Mix the saffron water with the melted butter. Set aside for basting.

Grill over a hot charcoal fire or under a very hot grill, turning once after 4 to 5 minutes when the underside has coloured. Baste with saffron butter. Turn and grill for 4 to 5 minutes more. The kebabs should be cooked through but still juicy. Add the tomato halves to the grill cut side down for the last 5 minutes.
Slide the kebabs off the skewers onto warmed flatbread. Serve with the grilled tomatoes, lemon halves, and saffron rice.

items.symptom: The meat keeps sliding off the skewer
items.cause: Mixture too wet or not kneaded enough
items.fix: Squeeze the onion more thoroughly. Knead for longer. Chill the mixture for an hour before skewering.

items.symptom: The kebabs are dry and crumbly
items.fix: Use fattier lamb mince. Cook for slightly less time; the meat should be just cooked through.
Season the raw mixture and taste a small fried patty before skewering. Adjust salt and pepper.

items.symptom: The surface is grey not charred
items.fix: The grill or coals must be very hot. Koobideh needs high direct heat to colour quickly without drying out.

content.text: Koobideh is the kebab of Iranian restaurants, street stalls, and home gardens across the country. It is the thing ordered by default, the benchmark by which every Iranian grill cook is judged. The pairing with chelow (saffron rice), grilled tomatoes, and raw onion is canonical. Eaten on a piece of flatbread stretched across the serving dish, the bread soaks up the meat juices and is eaten as a second course.
